overview: Zol's Mistake is the whole black north of Aoaz and every black island of the Kusmeel: a barren plateau of black rock, ash and black frost with a low ridge across it, cold, still and dim the year round, sparsely peopled and roamed by the dead. It takes its name from Zol, the Old God of Death, who came there long before Aen and Volgan, and nobody knows why the land is called a Mistake. Its working seat is the town of Furviatlon on the southern coast, whose keeper nobody knows; its only living people of whom anything is known are Leren-speaking fishers who winter on the outer isles nearest the North Lands. This file records what the charts, the fishers and the scholars of other lands have written about the Mistake, and nothing about who or what governs it, because nobody in Aoaz knows. The years in this data are the continuous count from Aen's victory that every regional history shares: a First Age year is itself, a Second Age year adds 1,675, a Third Age year adds 3,808 (taking the proposed Third Age of 1,260 years) and a Fourth Age year adds 5,068, so that 4A 1748 is year 6,816; a realm or place older than the numbered years carries 0, and every dated entry also gives its date as the world writes it, in the form 4A 1748. Everything not marked established is a proposal under the owner's decision L1.

ages.name: The Age of Kingdoms
ages.summary: Before Aen the black north was already desolate: Zol had come there long before Aen and Volgan, and no people of men lived in it or sailed near it that any chronicle remembers.

ages.name: The First Age
ages.summary: Zol's power in the north lay dormant through the First Age; the northern voyages charted the black coast and wrote its name, its lands sent no armies to anyone, and the old god of death took no part in the war against Volgan.

ages.name: The Second Age
ages.summary: In the Second Age the black north first stirred in any record, when the Great Necromancer drew on an old and terrible magic; sailors told of still seas and silent graves, and the scholars of the age argued about what it meant.

ages.name: The Third Age
ages.summary: Through the Order's age the black north kept its silence, and its only recorded sign came in the year of the Necromancer's fall, when the fishers say the sea lay still for a month; the length of 1,260 years is proposed.

countries.name: Zol's Mistake

founding.story: Zol, the Old God of Death and the only Old God in Aoaz, came to the black north long before Aen and Volgan, and the land was already a barren waste of black rock, ash and black frost when men first sailed near it. Nobody knows why it is called a Mistake. The year given is not the realm's beginning, which no one can date, but the year the northern voyages of the First Age first wrote the name on an Aenoran chart, beside a drawing of a still sea.

roots.story: What built the black north is the oldest silence in Aoaz, and every people who tells of it tells only what it saw from the sea. Zol, the Old God of Death, came there long before Aen and Volgan, and the land was already black rock, ash and black frost when the first sailors of the north-west came near it; their oldest sea-words, older than any chart, have a word for that coast that means only the shore from which nothing comes back. No people of men ever lived on the mainland in any memory, so the Mistake has no founder, no first king, no oath and no tongue of its own, and nobody knows why it is called a Mistake. What the living of the north keep instead is a custom. On the outer isles, before any Leren fisher wintered there, someone laid the dead inside rings of black stones and left every ring open on its northern side, and the fishers who came in 4A 230 found those rings older than any record and took up the custom as their own: the dead belong to the Old God of Death, they say, and a closed ring would be a theft from him. From that one belief come all the rest: the first fish of every season left on the black shore, the silence and the low lamps on still nights, the name never spoken at sea, and the winter tale of Kusven, the grave-wind who serves the Old God of Death, which the shore folk tell as a warning and no court takes for more than a tale. In 4A 1748 the open rings are still laid on Peledor, Drolkot and Erinlor, and the sailors who chart the Rim still draw them beside the still sea, because nothing the world has learned about the black north in four ages is more than that.

sign.device: Broken concentric rings in cold grey on a void-black field, each ring open on the same side: the sigil of the Will of Zol.
sign.origin: The sign first appears on an Aenoran chart of 1A 470, where a pilot of the northern voyages drew rings on flat water beside the name Zol's Mistake, broken where his pen lifted, as the mark of a sea that lay still and a coast where no bird followed the ships. When the Leren fishers came to the outer isles in 4A 230 they found the same figure laid on the black shore in stones, the burial rings of a people nobody remembers, each ring left open toward the north. Whose hand laid the first rings is not known, and the sign has no maker anyone can name: it belongs to the black north the way its silence does, and it is the sigil the charts and the courts give the Will of Zol, the emblem in whose name the realm is held.
sign.meaning: To the living it means the open ring of the dead: what dies is owed to the Old God of Death and is not kept from him. Raised over the hosts of the black north it threatens that every grave in their path is open, and that what they take does not come back.

dynasties.name: The Will of Zol
dynasties.notable: The charts and the courts name the realm's master only as the Will of Zol, because Zol has no body to sit on a throne and nobody living has seen who keeps his seat. Who administers Furviatlon for him is not known to any court, chronicle or fisherman.

events.name: The Name on the Chart
events.summary: Aenoran ships of the northern voyages chart the black coast and its islands and write the name Zol's Mistake beside them; the pilots' notes say the sea there was flat as a table and no bird followed the ships.

events.name: Nothing Sent to the Alliance
events.summary: When the Grand Alliance gathers against Volgan, the black north sends nothing to either side, and no faction can use its empty lands; the old god of death is not at Dardan.

events.name: The First Still Nights
events.summary: In the years when the Great Necromancer works toward Volgan's return, sailors of the Rim first tell of nights when the sea round the black isles lies still and every sound stops round the old graves of the coasts; the scholars of the Second Age argue about what woke and never agree.

events.name: The Still Month
events.summary: In the year the Great Necromancer falls, the fishers of the outer isles say the sea round the black isles lay still for a whole month and that they kept silent until it moved again; how the Necromancer fell is still argued.

events.name: The Outer Isles Fished
events.summary: Leren-speaking fishers from the North Lands begin to winter on the outer black isles nearest their own waters, where the cod run and the dead are fewest, and sell dried fish and seal in the northern harbours.

events.name: The Open Rings
events.summary: The first Leren fishers to winter on the outer isles find rings of black stones laid round old graves on the shore, every ring open on its northern side and older than any record; they bury their own dead the same way from that winter on, and the custom spreads to every isle they fish.

events.name: Ships Beyond the Rim
events.summary: In the long peace, ships that sail beyond the Rim toward the black isles do not always come back, and the Strait Litany of the North Lands begins to read the names of those lost there.

events.name: The Ring Closed at Erinlor
events.summary: A priest of the Strait Litany persuades a family of Erinlor to close the ring of their dead in the name of the twelve; the fishers say their boat was lost before the next still night, the ring is opened again by the neighbours, and no priest of the Litany has asked it of the isles since.

events.name: The Fishermen's Tale
events.summary: Fishermen of Orato and of the outer isles tell of black ships among the black isles of the Kusmeel; nobody in any royal court believes them.

rivalries.nature: The courts count the black north the old enemy of Aen's kingdom and do nothing about it, since nothing has come out of it in four ages.

countries.capitalReason: Furviatlon is the working seat because it is the one harbour on the Mistake's southern coast, at the mouth of the dark Furvi Run where a ship can land; who lives there, and who keeps it, nobody outside the Mistake can say.
countries.today: Zol's Mistake in 4A 1748 is silent: the Northern Wastes, the isle of Šodolôro and every black island of the Kusmeel, sparsely peopled and roamed by the dead, with perhaps 20,000 living souls, most of them Leren-speaking fishers on the outer isles who sell their catch in the North Lands and never go near Furviatlon. Fishermen tell of black ships among the isles; nobody at court believes them.

divergence.what: The dead of the black north come south through the islands and straits before the war of the West and the South begins.
divergence.consequence: The North Lands and the Dark Lands' northern shore face the dead alone and first, and the other wars of the age begin with every court already looking north.

divergence.what: The rising of the black north never comes in this age.
divergence.consequence: The War of the Last Crowns is a war of the living against Volgan and one another, and whatever stirs in the isles is left for the Fifth Age.

divergence.what: A court believes the fishermen and sends a ship to the black isles before 4A 1755.
divergence.consequence: If the ship comes back, its court is forewarned and arms its northern coasts; if it does not, the court believes the fishermen anyway.

divergence.what: The hosts of the black north and the hosts of the south destroy each other and never make common cause.
divergence.consequence: The living gain the time the two darks waste on each other, and the coalition of the living never faces them together.

divergence.what: The Strait Litany or a crown of the North Lands makes the fishers of the outer isles close the rings of their dead before the rising.
divergence.consequence: The fishers believe the black north will take its due another way and leave the outer isles, so nobody watches the Rim when the black ships put out, and the first coasts to be struck get no warning.

cities.name: Furviatlon
cities.legend: The northern fishers say smoke rises from Furviatlon on still nights and that nobody has ever seen a fire, and they steer wide of the Furvi Run's mouth because its water is said to be undrinkable to the living.
cities.economy: Nothing that any trader knows of; no ship of the living is recorded as having traded there.

cities.name: Šodolôro
cities.legend: On the great black oval of Šodolôro the fishers see walls and towers from the sea that look like a city, and they say no crew that put in there came back, so they steer round the isle by a day's sail.
cities.economy: Unknown; nothing living is known to dwell there.

cities.name: Peledor
cities.legend: The fishers of Peledor leave the first fish of every season on the black shore for whoever is listening, and they say the year a skipper ate it himself, his boat came home without him.
cities.economy: Cod and seal, dried on the black rock and sold in the North Lands' harbours.

cities.name: Drolkot
cities.legend: On still nights the folk of Drolkot keep silent and let their lamps burn low, because they hold that the god of the black north is listening, and a child who laughs on a still night is taken indoors.
cities.economy: Fishing, seal fat for the lamps, nets sold to Leren traders.

cities.name: Erinlor
cities.legend: The hamlet's founders came from a Leren harbour after a quarrel and swore never to go home; their grandchildren say the black isle keeps that oath for them, since no boat of Erinlor has ever found the way back south.
cities.economy: Fishing and egg-gathering on the cliffs, the poorest living of the outer isles.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The first fish
lawsAndCustoms.summary: The fishers of the outer isles leave the first fish of every season on the black shore, and believe that a skipper who keeps it will not keep his boat.

lawsAndCustoms.name: Silence on still nights
lawsAndCustoms.summary: When the sea round the isles falls still, the fishers keep silent, let the lamps burn low and do not put out, because they hold that the god of the black north is listening.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The name unspoken at sea
lawsAndCustoms.summary: Sailors of the North Lands hold it ill luck to name the Mistake at sea and call it only the black north, and the Strait Litany reads the names of the lost beyond the Rim.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The open rings
lawsAndCustoms.summary: The fishers of the outer isles bury their dead inside a ring of black stones and leave the ring open on its northern side, because the dead belong to the Old God of Death and a closed ring would keep from him what is his; the custom is older than their own wintering there, and nobody knows who began it.
